column1: # Routes for Felix itself.
# Not the generic template. Work on a governance harness divides differently
# from work on a product: there is no frontend and no deploy, and the dangerous
# change is an edit to something that runs in every session of every governed
# project. The constitution already calls that adversarial; this table is where
# that shows up before the work starts rather than during review.
# name
# Task-shape routes come FIRST, so they win a tie.
# They were below the subsystem rows, with a comment saying file order let a
# subsystem win — and that is backwards. A row says what the work is ABOUT; a
# task-shape row says what KIND of work it is, and the play depends far more on
# the kind. "debug why the harness hook is failing" scored harness and was told
# to go and brainstorm, while the debug row naming systematic-debugging sat
# below it and lost the tie. Four of ten rows lead with brainstorming and all
# four are subsystem rows, so any prompt naming a subsystem got the play for
# starting a new thing, whatever the turn was actually for.
debug
column2: debug broken failing crash traceback reproduce

column1: # `executing-plans` appended 2026-08-25. It is installed, it appears nowhere in
# this engine — not in any project table and not in the shipped template — and a
# blind study of 158 logged prompts found it was the capability wanted on three
# of the eight turns where anything was applicable at all. It was unnameable at
# any threshold by any matcher.
# Third, after writing-plans, because that is the sequence: brainstorm, write the
# plan, then work it. Appending costs no extra noise — felix_route_due names only
# the first unused step — and the sequence only began functioning tonight, since
# before the step-used fix every superpowers step read as already used and no
# play ever advanced past its first entry.
build
# Added 2026-08-13 from the misses, not from a guess about what work happens
# here. `merge` was the fourth most common word in prompts no row understood,
# and the top three above it were the project's own name and two pieces of
# conversation. Shipping is most of what a session ends on and had no row at
# all, so `code-review` was named by one route whose keywords nothing here says.
# `verification-before-completion` appended 2026-08-25, last, and from evidence
# rather than taste. The engine's own templates/routes.tsv ships a `release` row
# naming it. Felix's table replaced that row with `ship` and dropped the one
# capability that matters at the moment somebody says the work is done — so the
# Stop hook has been retrofitting it after the fact, twice in the session that
# noticed. Last in the play is the point: it comes due only once the review steps
# have actually run, which is when "is this really finished" is a real question
# rather than a rule quoted at turn one.
# `finishing-a-development-branch` removed 2026-09-13. Its procedure ends by
# presenting a person with a menu — merge, open a pull request, keep, discard —
# and Felix merges its own pull requests on green CI (the founder's direction,
# 2026-09-12). The stops that remain are felix merge's escape channels, a red
# gate, and the consent grants, none of which that menu is about.
ship

column1: # Narrowed 2026-08-18, from three misroutes reproduced in one session rather
# than from a guess. `review` matched "peer review" in a design conversation and
# demanded semgrep; `memory` matched "back the memory"; and `route` matched
# *misroute*, so a complaint about routing was routed as harness work. One
# mechanism: generic English words this project says constantly ABOUT itself,
# widened further by substring matching.
# The `review` row is now `security`, which is what it always was: its keywords
# are audit/vulnerabilit/injection/secret/credential and its play is a security
# audit. Renaming rather than deleting the keyword keeps the suite's rule that
# every route is reachable by its own name — a name you cannot summon is a lie —
# and "review this diff for injection" still lands here on `injection`.
# Narrowing is the safe direction because the cost is asymmetric. A missed route
# loses one suggestion. A false route arrives worded as a requirement, sends the
# session at the wrong work, and teaches it to read routing as noise — after
# which the correct routes stop working too.
# `orient` added 2026-09-10 from a measurement, not a guess. The knowledge
# graph under graphify-out/ had been built three times and queried once across
# 72 recorded sessions, and the once was the session in which the founder asked
# why it was never used. No row named it, so the ledger's `named` column for it
# read 0 in every session: a tool no route names cannot be pointed at, and its
# zero measured this table rather than the tool. The keywords are the words a
# structure question is actually asked with — who calls what, how the pieces
# fit. `trace` ties with `debug` on a traceback, and the file order above
# resolves that toward debugging, which is right. Placed above the subsystem
# rows so a question ABOUT the harness's shape wins over the play for changing
# it. Substring matching still applies: `calls` reaches "recalls", and if that
# misroutes in practice the fix is to narrow, per the note above.
orient
column2: orient graphify trace caller callers calls architecture codebase
